spans.s:
रोम 1. and 2. रोम, 1. and 2. रोमक, &c.
See col. 3.

1. रोम = रोमन् (at the end of an adj. comp., e. g.
अ-रोम, having no hair, hairless; cf. स-र्˚); (अस्),
m. a hole, cavity [cf. 1. रोप]; (अम्), n. water.

रोमन् रोमन्, अ, n. (probably fr. rt. 1. रुह्;
cf. लोमन्; according to Uṇādi-s.

. fr. rt.
[]
1. रु), the hair on the body of men and animals,
(especially) short hair, bristles, wool, down, nap, &c.,
(less properly applicable to the long hair on the head
and beard of men, and to that on the mane and tail
of animals); the feathers of a bird; (आणस्), m. pl.,
N. of a people; [cf. Hib. romach, ‘hairy;’ ro-
machad, ‘hairiness;’ roinfaith, ‘hair-cloth;’ roin,
roine, ‘hair, fur;’ roineach, ‘hairy.’]
—रोम-
कन्द, अस्, m. a kind of bulbous root or vegetable
(= पिण्डालु).
—रोम-कर्णक, अस्, m. ‘hair-eared,’
a hare.
—रोम-कूप, अस्, अम्, m. n. ‘hair-hole,’ a
pore of the skin; [cf. रोम-रन्ध्र.]
—रोम-
केसर, अम्, n. the tail of the Bos Grunniens
used as a Chowri, a whisk; (also written रोम-
केशर.)
—रोम-गर्त, अस्, m. = रोम-कूप.
—रोम-गुच्छ, अस्, m. or रोम-गुत्स, अम्,
n. the tail of the Bos Grunniens used as a
Chowri.
—रोमण्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. = रो-
म-वत्, covered with hair, hairy.
—रोम-त्यज्,
क्, क्, क्, Ved. losing the hair (said of a horse).
—रोम-पाद, अस्, m., N. of a king.
—रोम-
पुलक, अस्, m. the bristling of the hairs of the
body, a thrill of joy or fear (= रोम-हर्ष).
—रोम-फला, f. = रोमश-फल.
—रोम-
बद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘hair-bound,’ made or fastened
with the hair of animals, woven with hair.
—रोम-
बन्ध, अस्, m. hair-texture.
—रोम-भूमि, इस्,
f. the place of the hair, i. e. the skin.
—रोम-
मूर्धन्, आ, आ or ध्नी, अ, having short hairs on
the head, covered with hair or down on the head
(said of insects).
—रोम-रतासार, अस्, m. the
belly, (apparently a wrong form.)
—रोम-रन्ध्र,
अम्, n. a hole through which a hair shoots out, a
pore of the skin.
—रोम-राजि, इस्, or रोम-राजी, f.
a row or line of hair, a streak of hair (on the abdo-
men of men and especially of women just above the
navel, said to be a sign of puberty).
—रोम-राजि-
पथ, अस्, m. the line of the hair above the navel,
(in तनु-र्˚ = ‘the waist.’)
—रोम-लता or रोम-
लतिका, f. the winding line of hair above the navel
(of women).
—रोम-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessed of
hair, covered with hair, hairy, woolly.
—रोम-वाहिन्,
ई, इनी, इ, cutting off hair, sharp enough to cut a hair.
—रोम-विकार, अस्, m. or रोम-विक्रिया, f. change
of the hair of the body, bristling or erection of the
hair of the body, horripilation.
—रोम-विध्वंस,
अस्, m. ‘hair-destroying,’ a louse.
—रोम-विवर,
अम्, n. = रोम-कूप.
—रोम-वेध, अस्, m., N.
of an author.
—रोम-शुक, अम्, n. a kind of per-
fume.
—रोम-हर्ष, अस्, m. the bristling of the
hair of the body, a thrill or shudder (caused by joy,
fear, cold, &c.).
—रोम-हर्षण, अस्, ई, अम्,
causing the hair to bristle or stand erect, causing
excessive joy, causing a shudder or horror, awe-
inspiring, thrilling; (अस्), m. Terminalia Belerica
(the nuts of which are used as dice); N. of Sūta
(the pupil of Vyāsa and supposed narrator of the
events in the Purāṇas); N. of the father of Sūta;
(अम्), n. = रोम-हर्ष.
—रोम-हर्षित, अस्, आ,
अम्, thrilled with delight, having the hair of the
body bristling or erect with joy or horror.
—१. रो-
माञ्च (˚म-अञ्˚), अस्, m. ‘curling or erection of
the hair of the body,’ a thrill of rapture (= रोम-
हर्ष); thrill of horror, horripilation.
—२. रो-
माञ्च (fr. the preceding), Nom. P. रोमाञ्चति,
&c., to have the hair erect from excessive rapture,
to feel a thrill of joy or horror.
—रोमाञ्च-कञ्चुक,
अस्, m. a coat of mail consisting (as it were) of the
down of the body erect through delight.
—रोमाञ्-
चकिन्, ई, m., N. of a serpent-demon.
—रोमाञ्चिका,
f. a species of plant (= रुदन्ती).
—रोमाञ्चित, अस्,
आ, अम्, having the hair of the body erect or thrilled
with joy or horror, enraptured.
—रोमान्त (˚म-
अन्˚), अस्, m. the hairy side, i. e. the upper side of
the hand.
—रोमाली (˚म-आली), f. a row or line of
hair (above the navel; cf. रोम-राजि); = वयः-
सन्धि, (probably) puberty.
—रोमालु (˚म-आलु),
उस्, m. a sort of vegetable (= पिण्डालु).
—रोमालु-
विटपिन्, ई, m. a species of plant (= कुम्भी).
—रो-
मावली (˚म-आव्˚), f. a row or line of hair (above
the navel; cf. रोमाली).
—रोमाश्रय-फला (˚म-
[]
आश्˚), f. a species of shrub.
—रोमोद्गति (˚म-उद्˚),
इस्, f. or रोमोद्गम (˚म-उद्˚) or रोमोद्भेद
(˚म-उद्˚), अस्, m. erection of the hair (= रोम-
हर्ष, q. v.).
1. रोमक = रोमन् (at the end of an adj. comp.).

2. रोमक, अस्, m. Rome; ‘the Roman’ as epi-
thet of a particular astronomer; (आस्), m. pl., N. of
a people (mentioned in Mahā-bh. Sabhā-p. 1837;
cf. रोमाणस् under रोमन्); the people of the
Roman empire, the Romans; (अम्), n. a kind of
saline earth and the salt extracted from it; a kind
of magnet.
—रोमक-पत्तन, अम्, n. the city of
Rome.
—रोमक-सिद्धान्त, अस्, m., N. of one
of the five chief Siddhāntas in the age of Varāha-
mihira.
—रोमकाचार्य (˚क-आच्˚), अस्, m., N. of a
teacher of astronomy.

रोमश, अस्, आ, अम्, having thick hair, having
thick wool or bristles, hairy, woolly; (अस्), m. a
sheep, ram; a hog, boar; a sort of vegetable (=
पिण्डालु, कुम्भी); N. of a Ṛṣi; of an astro-
nomer [cf. 2. रोमक]; (आ), f. Cucumis Utilissi-
mus; N. of the reputed authoress of Ṛg-veda 1.
126, 7; (अम्), n. the pudenda (Ved.).
—रोमश-
फल, अस्, m. a species of plant (= टिण्डिश).
रोमकायण, अस्, m., N. of an author.

रोमन्थ रोमन्थ, अस्, m. (according to
some fr. रुज् + मन्थ), ruminating, chewing the
cud, (गगण-रोमन्थ, अस्, m. ‘ruminating on
the sky, ‘nonsense, absurdity); chewing; frequent
repetition; [cf. Gr. ἐρεύγομαι, ἐρυγγάνω,
ὀρυγγἀνω; Lat. rūmen (for rug-men), ruminare,
ructare; Old Germ. ita-ruchjan; Angl. Sax. roc-
cettan.]

रोमन्थाय, Nom. A. रोमन्थायते, &c., to
ruminate, chew the cud.

रोमन्थायमान, अस्, आ, अम्, ruminating, chew-
ing the cud.
